notes.meaning: God announces that He is revealing Himself to people who never looked for Him before. The apostle Paul explains that this speaks of the Gentiles—nations outside Israel—coming to know God through the gospel. God reaches out in mercy first, welcoming people into His family before they even think to ask.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read the verse as describing Israel's past neglect, arguing that God was making Himself available to His own covenant people who had behaved like pagans.

notes.meaning: God pictures Himself holding open His arms all day long like a loving father or an earnest speaker. Yet the people of Israel stubbornly refused His invitation, choosing to follow their own foolish desires instead. Walking by our own thoughts rather than God's guidance leads directly into rebellion.

The people insulted God right to His face without any shame or fear. They worshipped false gods in garden groves and built altars of brick instead of using the unhewn stone God commanded. Making up our own ways to worship directly defies the true God.

The people practiced dark rituals by sitting in tombs at night, trying to speak with the dead or receive visions from spirits. They also ate pork and drank broth made from unclean animals, breaking God's law and joining in pagan feasts. These practices made them spiritually and physically defiled in God's sight.

Even while committing these forbidden acts, these hypocrites warned others to keep away because they claimed to be holier than everyone else. God says their arrogant attitude is like irritating smoke constantly blowing into His nose. Self-righteous pride is utterly offensive to the Lord.

God declares that the sins of these rebels are written down in His heavenly records and will not be forgotten. He will not stay silent forever, but will certainly pay them back for their wrongdoing. The punishment will be poured right into their laps, meaning it will be personal, full, and unavoidable.

The Lord will judge both their own sins and the long-standing sins of their ancestors together. For generations, their fathers had insulted God by burning incense to idols on mountain hills instead of worshipping at His temple. God will settle the full account for this unbroken history of rebellion.

When a grape-picker finds a few good grapes in a withered cluster, someone says not to destroy the whole branch because there is still a blessing in it. In the same way, God promises that He will not destroy the entire nation. For the sake of His faithful servants—the godly remnant—He will spare a people for Himself.

God promises to bring forth true descendants from Jacob and heirs from the tribe of Judah. His chosen servants will inherit His holy mountain land and live there in safety. This points to the faithful believers who share in God's lasting inheritance.

Sharon on the western coast and the Valley of Achor in the east represent the entire land from border to border. Places that once experienced trouble and judgment will become rich pastures where herds rest in peace. God reserves these generous blessings for those who genuinely seek Him.

God turns His attention to those who abandoned Him and ignored His holy mountain in Jerusalem. Instead of trusting the Lord, they set feasts of food and poured spiced wine for the pagan gods of Fortune and Destiny. Looking to luck or false spirits is a direct betrayal of the living God.

Playing on the name of the idol Destiny, the Lord says He will destine these rebels to fall by the sword. This judgment comes because God called out to them through His prophets and they refused to listen or reply. They deliberately chose to do evil things that God detests.

The Lord draws a sharp contrast between His faithful servants and the unrepentant rebels. God's servants will feast, drink, and rejoice in His presence, while those who rejected Him will suffer hunger, thirst, and shame. Believers will sing with glad hearts, but the rebellious will cry out in agony and heartbreak.

The name of the wicked will become an example used in curses, a warning of how God judges the ungodly. The Lord will put these rebels to death, but He will give His true servants a brand-new name. This new name represents an honored identity and a place in God's family.

In that coming day, anyone asking for a blessing or taking an oath will do so by the God of truth. That title means the God of the 'Amen,' who always keeps His promises. All their past griefs and troubles will be completely forgotten and hidden from God's sight.

God promises to create new heavens and a new earth, bringing a complete renewal to the world. The pain and sorrows of the old world will fade away and never come to mind again. God's ultimate plan is to make all things new and beautiful for His people.

differ.view: This new creation begins spiritually in the gospel church through Christ and will be completed in the final eternal state after the last judgment.

notes.meaning: God commands His people to rejoice forever in the wonderful things He is creating. He will remake Jerusalem into a city full of celebration, and its people will be a source of pure delight. When God restores His community, sorrow is swallowed up in lasting joy.

The Lord Himself will take great joy in Jerusalem and delight in His people. The sounds of weeping, grief, and crying will never be heard in the city again. God loves His people so deeply that their happiness is His own delight.

Human life will be greatly lengthened, so that infants will not die young and old people will live out full lifespans. A person who dies at one hundred years old will be considered only a youth, while a sinner who dies at that age will be seen as cut down under a curse. Life under God's renewed blessing is filled with health and vitality.

differ.view: The prophet uses poetic language about long physical life to illustrate the spiritual fullness, peace, and victory over death found in the gospel and the heavenly city.

notes.meaning: God's people will build houses and live in them, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit. Cruel enemies will no longer invade and steal what they worked hard to produce. Their days will be as long as healthy trees, allowing them to fully enjoy everything their hands have made.

The people will not wear themselves out in useless work, nor will they raise children only to lose them to sudden disaster or war. They are a family blessed by the Lord, and their children will share in those blessings with them. God promises safety and a good future to their generations.

God promises that before His people even finish calling out, He will answer. While their requests are still on their lips, He is already listening and preparing help. This shows the wonderful closeness and instant communication believers enjoy with their heavenly Father.

The animal kingdom will live in perfect peace, with wolves and lambs grazing side by side and lions eating straw like cattle. The serpent will eat dust, showing that the power of evil remains completely defeated under God's ancient judgment. Nothing will hurt or destroy on all of God's holy mountain.
